title: Print the first three letters
description: Save a word in a variable. Use a slice with [ ] and : to print its first three letters.
hints: Read the task once and identify the Python feature it asks you to practise.
Use a slice with square brackets and a colon.
Write your own code, press Run, and fix any syntax or runtime error shown.
explanation: A slice [0:3] starts at index 0 and stops before index 3, so it returns the first three letters.
commonMistakes: The ending index is not included. Use [0:3], not [0:4], to get exactly three letters.

validation.feedback: Use a slice with square brackets and a colon.

title: Print a word backwards
description: Choose a word and use [::-1] to reverse it. Print the reversed word.
hints: Read the task once and identify the Python feature it asks you to practise.
Use a slice such as text[::-1] and print the reversed text.
Write your own code, press Run, and fix any syntax or runtime error shown.
explanation: [::-1] reads the characters from the end to the beginning. Python becomes nohtyP.
commonMistakes: Use a word that is not the same forwards and backwards, then use [::-1].

validation.feedback: Use a slice such as text[::-1] and print the reversed text.
